9. Pazopanib / Venous Thromboembolic Events 
 
 
 
                     ________    ________  
Alert Message:  Venous thromboembolic events (VTEs) have been reported with the use of  
Votrient (pazopanib).  In the renal cell carcinoma (RCC) clinical trial, VETs occurred in 1% of  
290 patients treated with pazopanib.  In the soft tissue sarcoma trial (STS), VTEs were reported  
in 5% of 240 patients, and fatal pulmonary embolism (PE) was reported in 1% of 240 patients.   
Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of VTE and PE.  For Grade 3 VET, withhold pazopanib  
and resume at the same dose if managed with appropriate therapy for at least one week.   
Permanently discontinue pazopanib in case of Grade 4 VTE. 
 
Drugs/Diseases 
Util A

10. Pazopanib / Thrombotic Microangiopathy

Votrient (pazopanib).  Monitor patients for signs and symptoms of TMA.  Permanently discontinue  
pazopanib in patients developing TMA.

11. Pazopanib / Interstitial Lund Disease/Pneumonitis 
 
 
                     ________    ________  
Alert Message:  Interstitial Lung Disease/Pneumonitis (ILD)/pneumonitis, which can be fatal,  
has been reported with Votrient (pazopanib) across clinical trials.  Monitor patients for signs and  
symptoms of ILD/ pneumonitis.  Permanently discontinue pazopanib in patients who develop

12. Pazopanib / Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome 
 
                     ________    ________  
Alert Message:  Posterior Reversible Encephalopathy Syndrome (PRES) has been reported in  
patients who received Votrient (pazopanib).  PRES is a neurologic disorder that can present  
with headache, seizures, lethargy, confusion, visual, and neurologic disturbances.  PRES can  
be fatal.  Permanently discontinue pazopanib in patients who develop PRES.

13. Pazopanib / Gastrointestinal Perforation & Fistula 
 
 
                     ________    ________  
Alert Message:  Votrient (pazopanib) can cause gastrointestinal perforation and fistula, some  
fatal.  Monitor the patient for signs and symptoms of gastrointestinal perforation and fistula.   
Withhold pazopanib in case of Grade 2 or 3 gastrointestinal fistula and resume based on  
medical judgment.  Permanently discontinue pazopanib in case of gastrointestinal perforation  
or Grade 4 gastrointestinal fistula.

14. Pazopanib / Strong CYP3A4 Inhibitors  
 
 
 
                     ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  Avoid the concurrent use of Votrient (pazopanib) with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 
Pazopanib is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors can  
cause increased pazopanib concentrations and risk of pazopanib-related adverse effects.   
Consider an alternate concomitant medication with no or minimal enzyme-inhibiting potential.   
If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the dose of pazopanib to 400 mg once daily.

16. Pazopanib / CYP3A4, 2D6, & 2C8 Substrates with NTI 
 
 
                     ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  The concomitant use of Votrient (pazopanib) with medications with narrow  
therapeutic windows that are metabolized by CYP3A4, CYP2D6, or CYP2C8 is not recommended. 
Pazopanib is an inhibitor of CYP3A4-, CYP2D6-, and CYP2C8-mediated metabolism.  Concurrent  
use of pazopanib with agents that are CYPA4, CYP2D6, or CY2C8 substrates with narrow  
therapeutic windows may result in the inhibition of the metabolism of these agents, increased  
plasma concentrations, and potential for serious adverse reactions.

19. Pazopanib / H2 Blockers & PPIs 
  
 
 
   
                     ________    ________     
Alert Message:  The concurrent use of Votrient (pazopanib) with gastric acid-reducing agents  
should be avoided.  Pazopanib displays pH-dependent solubility with decreased solubility at  
higher pH.  If concomitant administration with a gastric acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided,  
consider short-acting antacids in place of PPIs and H2-receptor antagonists.  Separate  
short-acting antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours to avoid a reduction in pazopanib  
exposure.

20. Pazopanib / Pregnancy / Pregnancy Negating  
 
 
                     ________    ________  
Alert Message:   Based on animal reproductive studies and its mechanism of action, Votrient  
(pazopanib) can cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.  In animal  
developmental and reproductive toxicology studies, oral administration of pazopanib to  
pregnant rats and rabbits throughout organogenesis resulted in teratogenicity, and abortion at  
system exposures lower than that observed at the MRHD.  Advise pregnant women of the  
potential risk to a fetus.

 27. Lazertinib / Venous Thromboembolic Events  
 
 
                     ________    ________  
Alert Message: Lazcluze (lazertinib) in combination with amivantamab can cause serious and  
fatal venous thromboembolism events (VTE), including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary  
embolism.  Monitor for signs and symptoms of VTE.  If a Grade 2 or 3 VTE occurs, withhold  
lazertinib and amivantamab and initiate anticoagulant therapy.  Once anticoagulant therapy  
has been initiated, resume the combination therapy at the prior dose level.  For Grade 4 VTE 
or recurrent Grade 2 or 3 VTE, withhold lazertinib, permanently discontinue amivantamab,  
and initiate anticoagulant therapy.  Once anticoagulant therapy has been initiated, resume the  
lazertinib therapy at the same dose level.  
 
Drugs/Diseases

28. Lazertinib / Interstitial Lund Disease/Pneumonitis 
 
 
                     ________    ________  
 
Alert Message:  Lazcluze (lazertinib) in combination with amivantamab can cause interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis 
(ILD)/pneumonitis.  Monitor patients for signs and symptoms indicative of  
ILD/ pneumonitis (e.g., dyspnea, cough, fever).  Immediately withhold both lazertinib and  
amivantamab in patients with suspected (ILD)/pneumonitis and permanently discontinue if  
ILD/pneumonitis is confirmed.

29. Lazertinib / Dermatologic Adverse Reactions 
 
 
 
                     ________    ________

31. Lazertinib / Strong CYP3A4 Inducers  
 
 
 
                     ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  Lazcluze (lazertinib) is a CYP3A4 substrate, and concurrent use with a strong  
or moderate CYP3A4 inducer can decrease lazertinib concentrations, which may reduce the  
efficacy of lazertinib.  Avoid the concomitant use of lazertinib with strong and moderate CYP3A4  
inducers.

45. Vanzacaftor/Tezacaftor/Deutivacaftor / Strong 3A Inhibitors ≥ 12 yoa 
                     ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  Concomitant use of Alyftrek (vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor) with strong  
CYP3A inhibitors may require dosage reduction of the fixed-dose combination medication.   
The dose of vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor when used concurrently with a strong CYP3A  
inhibitor in patients 12 years of age and older is one vanzacaftor 10 mg/tezacaftor 50  
mg/deutivacaftor 125 mg tablet once a week.  All three components of the combination  
product are substrates of CYP3A, and concomitant use with a strong CYP3A inhibitor may  
result in increased exposure to all components and risk of vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor-related  
adverse effects.

50.  Vanzacaftor/Tezacaftor/Deutivacaftor / Pregnancy / Pregnancy Negating                     ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  There are no available data on Alyftrek (vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor) 
use in pregnant women to evaluate for a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage,  
or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.  There are animal studies that have been  
conducted separately with vanzacaftor, tezacaftor, and ivacaftor (deutivacaftor is the deuterated  
isotopologue of ivacaftor).  No adverse developmental effects were observed after oral  
administration of vanzacaftor, tezacaftor, or ivacaftor to pregnant rats from the period of  
organogenesis through lactation at doses that produced maternal exposures approximately 18  
times, 1 time, and 8 times the exposures at the MRHD, respectively.  Placental transfer of  
vanzacaftor, tezacaftor, and ivacaftor was observed in pregnant rats.

51. Vanzacaftor/Tezacaftor/Deutivacaftor / Lactation 
 
 
                     ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  There are no data on the presence of Alyftrek (vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor)  
in human milk, the effects on the breastfed infant, or the effects on milk production.  Vanzacaftor,  
tezacaftor, and ivacaftor (deutivacaftor is the deuterated isotopologue of ivacaftor) are excreted into  
the milk of female rats.  When a drug is present in animal milk, it is likely that the drug will be present  
in human milk.  The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along  
with the mother’s clinical need for vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor and any potential adverse  
effects on the breastfed child from vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor or the underlying maternal  
condition.

54. Inavolisib / Overuse   
 
                              
 
                     ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  Itovebi (inavolisib) may be over-utilized.  The recommended dosage of inavolisib  
for patients with moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30 to < 60 mL/min based on CKD-EPI) is 6  
mg once daily.  In pharmacokinetic studies, the AUC was 73% higher in patients with moderate  
renal impairment compared to patients with normal renal function. Inavolisib has not been  
evaluated in patients with severe renal impairment.  No dosage adjustment is recommended in  
patients with mild renal impairment.

56. Inavolisib / Hyperglycemia 
 
    
 
 
 
                    ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  Itovebi (inavolisib) can cause severe hyperglycemia.  After initiating inavolisib,  
monitor or have the patient self-monitor fasting glucose levels once every 3 days for the first  
week, then once every week for the next 3 weeks, then once every 2 weeks for the next 8  
weeks, and then once every 4 weeks thereafter.   Manage hyperglycemia with anti-hyperglycemic  
medications as clinically indicated.  Based on the severity of hyperglycemia, inavolisib may  
require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation.

58. Inavolisib / Diarrhea  
 
 
 
 
 
                     ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  Severe diarrhea, including dehydration and acute kidney injury, can occur in  
patients treated with Itovebi (inavolisib). In clinical trials, diarrhea occurred in 48% of patients  
receiving inavolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant.  Monitor patients for signs and symptoms  
of diarrhea.  Advise the patient to increase oral fluids and start antidiarrheal treatment at the  
first sign of diarrhea while taking inavolisib.  Withhold, reduce the dose, or permanently  
discontinue inavolisib based on the severity of diarrhea.

59. Inavolisib / Pregnancy / Pregnancy Negating 
 
 
 
                     ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  Based on animal data and its mechanism of action, Itovebi (inavolisib) can  
cause fetal harm when administered to a pregnant woman.  In an animal reproductive study,  
oral administration of inavolisib to pregnant rats during organogenesis caused adverse  
developmental outcomes, including structural abnormalities and embryo-fetal mortality.   
Advise pregnant women and females of reproductive potential of the potential risk to a fetus.

68. Sparsentan / Hepatic Impairment – Box Warning 
 
 
 
       ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  Filspari (sparsentan) may cause hepatotoxicity.  Advise patients with symptoms  
suggesting hepatotoxicity to immediately stop treatment with sparsentan and seek medical  
attention.  If aminotransferase levels are abnormal at any time during treatment, interrupt  
sparsentan and monitor as recommended.  Avoid initiation of sparsentan in patients with  
elevated aminotransferases, as these patients may be at increased risk for serious  
hepatotoxicity.

69. Sparsentan / Acute Kidney Injury 
 
 
 
 
 
       ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  Filspari (sparsentan) may cause acute kidney failure, and periodic kidney  
function monitoring is recommended during treatment with sparsentan.  Sparsentan is  
an endothelin and angiotensin II receptor antagonist, and drugs that inhibit the  
renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) can adversely affect the kidneys.  Patients  
whose kidney function may depend in part on the activity of the renin-angiotensin system  
(e.g., patients with renal artery stenosis, chronic kidney disease, severe congestive heart  
failure or volume depletion) may be at particular risk of developing acute kidney injury.

72. Sparsentan / Strong CYP3A Inhibitors  
 
 
 
 
       ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  The use of Filspari (sparsentan) with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. 
Sparsentan is a CYP3A substrate, and concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors may  
increase sparsentan Cmax and AUC, which may increase the risk of sparsentan-related adverse  
reactions.  If the use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor cannot be avoided, interrupt treatment with  
sparsentan.  When resuming treatment with sparsentan, consider dose titration (initial treatment 
with sparsentan at 200 mg once daily, after 14 days, increase to the recommended dose of 400  
mg once daily, as tolerated).

79. Sparsentan / Lactation 
 
 
    
 
 
 
       ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  There are no data on the presence of Filspari (sparsentan) in human milk, the  
effects on the breastfed infant, or the effect on milk production.  Because of the potential for  
adverse reactions, such as hypotension in breastfed infants, advise patients not to breastfeed  
during treatment with sparsentan.

80. Sparsentan / Therapeutic Appropriateness 
    
 
 
 
       ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective contraception before  
initiation of treatment, during treatment, and for 2 weeks after discontinuation of sparsentan.   
Sparsentan can cause fetal harm if used by pregnant patients.

82. Fremanezumab-vfrm / Overuse  
 
 
                              
       ________    ________     
 
Alert Message:  Ajovy (fremanezumab-vfrm) may be over-utilized.  The recommended dosage  
of fremanezumab-vfrm for the preventive treatment of episodic migraine in pediatric patients  
who are 6 to 17 years of age and who weigh 45 kg or more is 225 mg monthly.

83. Dihydroergotamine 0.725 Nasal / Overuse  
 
                              
    ________    ________ 
 
Alert Message:  Trudhesa (dihydroergotamine nasal spray) may be over-utilized.  The  
recommended dose of nasal dihydroergotamine is 1.45 mg administered as two metered  
sprays (one 0.725 mg spray in each nostril).  The dose may be repeated, if needed, a  
minimum of 1 hour after the first dose.  Do not use more than 2 doses of dihydroergotamine  
nasal spray within 24 hours or 3 doses within a 7-day period. 
 
Drugs/Diseases 
Util A
